newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: ATHLETICS-BIG WELCOME FOR ATHENS MEDALIST.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BIG WELCOME FOR ATHENS MEDALIST.

text.p: Sri Lanka laid out a red carpet welcome on Tuesday for sprinter Susanthika Jayasinghe, who won the 200 meters silver medal at the World athletics championships in Athens last week.

Jayasinghe, only the second Sri Lankan in nearly 50 years to win a medal in a major world championship, was driven in a convoy of vehicles while thousands of people lined the streets from the airport to cheer her with flags and banners.
Jayasinghe was scheduled to be feted by President Chandrika Bandaranaike Kumaratunga later in the day.
The only other Sri Lankan to ever win a medal was Duncan White, who picked up the silver in 400 meters hurdles at the 1948 Olympics in London.
Jayasinghe clocked 22.39 seconds to win her medal, defeating favourite Jamaican Merlene Ottey. The gold went to Ukrainian Zhanna Pintussevich.
Sports Minister S.B. Dissanayake told local newspapers that Jayasinghe will be given one million rupees in cash or property as a gift.
Other awards, from the government and corporate houses, were also expected for the island's new sprint queen after Sri Lankan cricketers were gifted plots of lands for creating new world records.
Sri Lanka made the highest ever test score of 952 for six against India last week at Colombo, beating England's 59 year-old record.
